question: What prerequisite subjects are required for MSDS admission, and what programming background is generally expected?
expected_answer_points: Calculus I and Linear Algebra are required, or their equivalents.
An introductory Computer Science or equivalent CS-101 programming course is required.
One of Calculus II, Probability, Statistics, or an advanced physics, engineering, or econometrics course with heavy mathematical content is required.
There is no fixed programming-language requirement, but serious academic or professional experience with Python and/or R is generally expected.

evidence.quote:
To be considered for the program, you must have completed the following (or equivalents, e.g., MOOCs certification or course credit):

Calculus I: limits, derivatives, series, integrals, etc.
Linear Algebra

Intro to Computer Science (or an equivalent “CS-101” programming course): We have no set requirements regarding specific languages, but we generally expect serious academic and/or professional experience with Python and/or R at a minimum.
One of Calculus II, Probability, Statistics, or an advanced physics, engineering, or econometrics course with heavy mathematical content

scoring_notes: Do not present every subject in the final prerequisite group as mandatory; it is a choice of one. Distinguish expected programming experience from a fixed language requirement.

question: I work full-time. What semester workload does the admissions FAQ suggest, are evening classes guaranteed, and does continuous enrollment also apply in summer?
expected_answer_points: The admissions FAQ suggests 6 or fewer credits per semester for students with a full-time job.
Evening scheduling is not guaranteed; working students need flexibility to take required daytime courses.
Continuous enrollment is required every fall and spring semester, but not in summer.

evidence.anchor: Can I work full-time while taking classes?
evidence.quote: The suggested full-time program is 9 credits per semester. Because of the heavy workload, 9 credits will equal out to about 40 hours of work per week. Students should be able to work while taking classes, but due to the amount of work required for the program, we suggest taking 6 or fewer credits per semester if you have a full-time job. We try to schedule required courses in the evenings, but this is not guaranteed. Full-time working students should have the flexibility to take required courses during the daytime if needed.

evidence.anchor: Are students required to take courses every semester?
evidence.quote: Students are required to be continuously enrolled every fall and spring semester. If there is a semester where you do not want to take courses, please reach out to CDS-masters@nyu.edu to discuss options. This requirement does not apply to the summer semester.

scoring_notes: The 6-credit suggestion is a recommendation, not a universal enrollment maximum. For the summer point, explicitly stating that continuous enrollment does not apply in summer is sufficient; naming both fall and spring is optional.

question: For Fall 2027, how many Pathbreaker scholarships are described, what do they cover, and is a separate application required?
expected_answer_points: The page describes scholarships for two Fall 2027 MS students.
They cover full tuition for the MSDS, described as 36 points of tuition and fees support.
Applying to the CDS MS program automatically places applicants under consideration; a separate scholarship application is not required.

evidence.quote: In our commitment to foster innovation in data science, we launched the CDS Pathbreaker Scholarship in 2024. To support this mission, we are offering scholarships for two Fall 2027 MS students, covering the full tuition for our Master’s of Science in Data Science degree. That’s 36 points of tuition and fees support.

Students need only to apply for the CDS MS program to be automatically considered for the scholarship. While not mandatory, applicants who believe they qualify for the Pathbreaker are encouraged to highlight their experiences in the personal statement section of the MS application.

scoring_notes: Keep the Fall 2027 cohort explicit. Do not substitute the historical launch year or counts of past recipients, or promise that every applicant receives an award.

question: How do the admissions FAQ and Industry Concentration page describe internship timing, and what advice does the concentration page give international students?
expected_answer_points: The admissions FAQ describes CPT as paid internships for credit after the first year of the degree.
The Industry Concentration page specifies a mandatory internship within the first year.
For that concentration, international students are directed to NYU’s Office of Global Services about obtaining early CPT status within their first year.

evidence.anchor: Will CPT or OPT be offered?
evidence.quote: Yes, CPT and OPT are options for Data Science students. CPT is “curricular practical training,” a program which allows international students to obtain paid internships for credit after the first year of the degree.

evidence.anchor: Master’s in Data Science: Industry Concentration
evidence.quote: CDS offers the Industry Concentration for the MS in Data Science. This concentration is specifically designed to respond to the needs and inputs from companies, allowing MS in Data Science students to apply the knowledge and skills obtained in their coursework to industry-related projects during the degree program. It requires more industry-targeted coursework and a Practical Training experience, including a mandatory internship within the first year of study. International students should consult NYU’s Office of Global Services on how to obtain early CPT status within their first year if pursuing this concentration.

scoring_notes: Attribute each timing statement to its page and context. Do not erase either statement, declare personal visa eligibility, or claim that one page supersedes the other.
